questions.q: The Weights and Measures Department protects consumers mainly by
options: checking that scales and measures used in markets are accurate
fixing the prices of essential commodities
questions.explanation: The department ensures weighing and measuring devices are accurate so buyers get the quantity paid for. Fixing prices, issuing import licences and registering trademarks are handled by other bodies or are not its core function.

questions.q: A consumer in Port Harcourt checks the label of a canned drink before buying it. Which information on the label most directly guards against buying an unsafe, expired product?
questions.explanation: The expiry date shows the last date the drink is expected to be safe and suitable for consumption. Brand name, net weight and manufacturer's address do not directly show whether the product has expired.

questions.q: A trader in Enugu deposits ₦250,000 in a fixed deposit account at 6% simple interest per annum for 15 months. How much interest does she earn?
questions.explanation: Simple interest = ₦250,000 × 6/100 × 15/12 = ₦18,750. The amount ₦15,000 would be the interest for only one year, not for 15 months.

questions.q: A firm in Kano that makes industrial sewing machines prefers personal selling to advertising because the machines are costly and each buyer needs detailed explanation. This choice is mainly because personal selling
options: reaches a very large mass market at low cost
removes the need for after-sales service
allows direct interaction and negotiation with the buyer
guarantees that the product will not be imitated
questions.explanation: Personal selling puts a salesperson in direct contact with each buyer, so the machine can be explained and terms negotiated. Advertising is better for reaching a mass market cheaply, and personal selling does not remove after-sales service or prevent imitation.

questions.q: A company in Aba sells its shoes through selected reputable retailers in major cities instead of making them available in every shop. This distribution strategy is called
questions.explanation: Selective distribution uses a limited number of chosen outlets rather than every possible shop. Intensive distribution aims at as many outlets as possible, while exclusive distribution usually gives one outlet the sole right in an area.

questions.q: A Nigerian exporter in Aba receives payment in US dollars from a buyer in the United States. He exchanges the dollars for naira at a commercial bank. The market where this exchange takes place is the
questions.explanation: The foreign exchange market is where one currency is exchanged for another, such as US dollars for naira. The capital market deals in long-term securities, while the money market handles short-term funds and the commodity market deals in raw materials.

questions.q: Ngozi owns a tailoring business in Enugu. She uses her sewing machines, cutting table and pressing iron to make school uniforms. In production, these items are classified as
questions.explanation: Sewing machines, a cutting table and a pressing iron are man-made resources used to produce goods, so they are capital. Land refers to natural resources, labour is human effort, and entrepreneurship is the organisation and risk-bearing function.

questions.q: Dr. Bello attends to patients at a clinic in Ilorin and is paid for his service. The service he renders is an example of
questions.explanation: A doctor providing treatment directly to a patient is rendering a personal service to the final consumer, which is a direct service. Indirect services assist trade and production, while primary production and manufacturing involve goods rather than this type of personal service.

questions.q: Musa works as a machine operator in a tyre factory in Benin City. In which sector of production is his occupation classified?
questions.explanation: Working in a tyre factory is manufacturing, which is a secondary production activity that transforms raw materials into finished goods. Primary and extractive activities involve obtaining raw materials directly from nature, while tertiary activities provide services.

questions.q: A trader in Ibadan carries household goods from street to street and sells directly to residents. This type of retailing is called
questions.explanation: Hawking involves moving from place to place to sell goods directly to consumers. Mail order and automatic vending sell through other methods, while multiple shop retailing uses several fixed branches owned by one organisation.

questions.q: A wholesaler in Kano gives a retailer a reduction of ₦200 per carton from the list price on goods bought for resale. This reduction is known as
questions.explanation: A trade discount is a reduction from the list price allowed to buyers in the trade, especially for buying in bulk or for resale. A cash discount is given for prompt payment, commission is paid to an agent, and mark-up is an addition to cost.

questions.q: Crude oil and natural gas are moved continuously from production fields to refineries and markets in Nigeria with little human labour by using
questions.explanation: Pipeline transport is suitable for moving liquids and gases continuously over long distances with minimal labour. Air, rail and road transport are not used for continuous mass movement of crude oil and natural gas in this way.

questions.q: A sales manager in Lagos sends a text message to a customer and the customer replies, 'Received, thank you.' In the communication process, the customer's reply is the
questions.explanation: Feedback is the receiver's response to the sender's message, and in this case the customer's reply confirms receipt. Encoding is the conversion of an idea into a message, the medium is the channel used, and noise is any interference with the message.

questions.q: A trader in Aba returns damaged cartons of goods to a supplier in Onitsha. Which document will the supplier most appropriately issue to reduce the amount owed by the trader?
questions.explanation: A credit note is issued by a seller to reduce the amount owed by a buyer when goods are returned or an overcharge is corrected. A debit note would increase or record an amount due, while a pro forma invoice is only a quotation or advance invoice.

questions.q: An exporter in Kano wishes to satisfy customs authorities in another country that the goods being shipped were produced in Nigeria. Which document should the exporter obtain?
questions.explanation: A certificate of origin is the document that declares the country in which goods were produced, and customs authorities may require it for tariff or import purposes. A commercial invoice shows prices and payment terms, while a packing list describes the packages and contents.

questions.q: A public company in Ibadan wants to raise fresh capital by offering shares to the public. Which institution is appointed to advise on and manage the issue for a fee?
questions.explanation: An issuing house, often a merchant bank, advises on and manages new securities issues for companies raising capital from the public. A stockbroker buys and sells shares on behalf of clients, while a registrar maintains the company's register of shareholders.

questions.q: An investor bought 500 ordinary shares of a company at ₦8.00 per share. The company later declared a dividend of 50 kobo per share. What is the dividend yield based on the purchase price?
questions.explanation: The dividend per share is 50 kobo, which is ₦0.50. Dividend yield = (₦0.50 ÷ ₦8.00) × 100% = 6.25%.

questions.q: A state ministry in Enugu purchases office stationery from a registered online supplier. This electronic transaction is best described as:
questions.explanation: Business-to-government e-commerce occurs when a business sells goods or services online to a government agency. Business-to-business involves transactions between companies, while consumer-to-consumer involves individuals trading with one another.

questions.q: An online buyer in Abuja pays for goods through a service that holds the money until the seller's goods are delivered and accepted. This payment arrangement is called:
questions.explanation: Escrow is an arrangement in which a neutral third party holds the buyer's payment until the agreed conditions, such as delivery and acceptance of goods, are met. An electronic wallet stores funds, while a chargeback is a reversal of a card payment after a dispute.

questions.q: A trader in Kano pays an annual premium of ₦45,000 for a fire policy with a sum insured of ₦1,500,000. What is the premium rate per cent?
questions.explanation: Premium rate per cent = (₦45,000 ÷ ₦1,500,000) × 100% = 3%. The value 33.33% comes from reversing the ratio instead of dividing premium by sum insured.

questions.q: A shopper in Ibadan checks the expiry date and seal of a tin of milk before paying for it. This action best illustrates a consumer's
questions.explanation: Checking expiry dates and seals is part of a consumer's duty to exercise care before buying. Rights such as redress and being heard arise when a complaint or loss occurs, while choice concerns selecting among available products.

questions.q: The main purpose of regulating advertisements in Nigeria is to
questions.explanation: Advertising regulation aims to prevent false or misleading advertisements that could deceive buyers. It is not intended to raise advertising costs, create monopolies, or fund advertising agencies.

questions.q: A manufacturer of a generator in Lagos gives a one-year warranty with each unit sold. The main purpose of the warranty is to
options: guarantee that the product will never develop any fault
transfer ownership of the product to the manufacturer after the period
assure the buyer of repair or replacement for manufacturing defects within the stated period
prevent the buyer from reselling the product during the period
questions.explanation: A warranty is a manufacturer's promise to repair or replace a product with a manufacturing defect within a stated period. It does not promise that no fault will ever occur, restrict resale, or transfer ownership.

questions.q: Musa has a current account with a bank in Kano. After a written arrangement with the bank, he is allowed to withdraw up to ₦50,000 beyond the balance in his account. This facility is called
questions.explanation: An overdraft is an arrangement permitting a current account holder to withdraw beyond the credit balance up to an agreed limit. A fixed deposit is money kept for a period, a standing order is a regular payment instruction, and a bank draft is a payment instrument.

questions.q: A supplier in Lagos draws a bill of exchange on a bank in Abuja. The bank writes on the bill that it will pay the amount when due. By doing this, the bank has
questions.explanation: Acceptance occurs when the drawee of a bill signs or writes on it agreeing to pay it at maturity. Endorsement transfers the bill by the holder, while discounting is selling it to a bank before maturity.

questions.q: When the Central Bank of Nigeria prints and puts new naira notes and coins into circulation, it is performing the function of
options: acting as lender of last resort
questions.explanation: The Central Bank of Nigeria has the sole authority to issue legal tender, so printing and circulating new naira notes and coins is currency issue. Lending to the government, acting as lender of last resort, and clearing cheques are different central banking functions.

questions.q: A beverage company in Ibadan wants to know why sales of its new drink fell in some areas. It collects opinions from retailers and consumers and analyses its sales records. This activity is called
questions.explanation: Market research is the systematic collection and analysis of information about customers, competitors, and sales to guide marketing decisions. Segmentation divides a market into groups, sales promotion stimulates buying, and public relations seeks goodwill.

questions.q: A company in Aba manufactures heavy industrial machines that are bought by only a few large factories. The most suitable medium for advertising these machines is
questions.explanation: Trade journals are specialised publications that reach a particular industry, making them suitable for expensive industrial machines bought by a few factories. Radio, television, and roadside posters are mass media better suited to widely consumed goods.

questions.q: One major disadvantage of a sole proprietorship is that
options: profits are shared among many owners
the business cannot employ paid workers
the owner bears unlimited liability for the debts of the business
questions.explanation: A sole proprietor has no separate legal personality, so personal assets can be used to settle business debts. The owner normally keeps the profits and can make decisions quickly, and the business may employ paid workers.

questions.q: A public corporation is best described as a business organisation that is
options: owned by members who share profits according to patronage
owned by the government and set up by law to provide essential services
formed by two or more persons with a maximum of twenty partners
owned by private shareholders and run for profit
questions.explanation: A public corporation is a statutory body owned by government and established by law to provide essential goods or services to the public. It is not owned by private shareholders, a cooperative membership, or a partnership.

questions.q: A Nigerian insurance company receives a premium from a Ghanaian shipping firm for insuring its cargo. This transaction is recorded in Nigeria's foreign trade as
questions.explanation: The premium is payment for an insurance service sold by a Nigerian firm to a foreign shipping firm, so it is an invisible export. Visible exports involve tangible goods, while an invisible import would be a service bought from abroad; a unilateral transfer is a gift or remittance without a service in return.

questions.q: Which of the following documents is completed by an importer to declare imported goods to the customs authorities and determine the duty payable?
questions.explanation: The bill of entry is the customs declaration used by an importer when goods arrive and it provides the basis for calculating import duty. A bill of lading is a carriage document, a certificate of origin shows where goods were produced, and a pro forma invoice is a preliminary price quotation.

questions.q: A group of small retailers in Kano buys goods directly from manufacturers in large quantities and shares the goods among its members at cost. This arrangement is best described as
questions.explanation: A retailers' buying cooperative pools members' orders to buy in bulk from manufacturers and then shares the goods at cost. A multiple shop is a chain of branches under one ownership, a department store has separate sections under one roof, and a mail-order business sells through catalogues or post.

questions.q: Which of the following services does a wholesaler render to a manufacturer?
options: Providing after-sales repair services to households
Selling goods in small quantities to final consumers
Storing goods in bulk until retailers demand them
Collecting payment directly from final consumers on behalf of retailers
questions.explanation: A wholesaler helps the manufacturer by holding goods in bulk and releasing them as retailers demand them, which reduces the manufacturer's storage burden. Selling to final consumers and providing after-sales repairs to households are retail functions, not services a wholesaler normally provides to a manufacturer.

questions.q: Which of the following is a major disadvantage of air transport to a Nigerian trader who imports bulky goods?
options: It is unsuitable for valuable and light goods.
It cannot operate between international destinations.
It is too slow for perishable goods.
The freight charges are relatively high.
questions.explanation: Air transport is fast and suitable for perishable or high-value light goods, but its freight charges are high, which makes it costly for bulky imports. The statements that it is slow, cannot operate internationally, or is unsuitable for valuable light goods are incorrect.

questions.q: A beverage company in Abeokuta pays for airtime on a radio station to announce a new price for its product. In the communication process, the radio station serves as the
questions.explanation: The radio station is the medium, the means by which the company's encoded announcement is transmitted to listeners. Feedback is the response received, a receiver is the party for whom the message is intended, and noise is any interference in the communication process.

questions.q: Which of the following is a primary occupation?
options: A fisherman in Bayelsa catching fish from the river
A bank cashier in Enugu receiving deposits
A bus driver in Lagos conveying passengers
A tailor in Aba sewing shirts for customers
questions.explanation: Fishing directly takes a natural resource from water, which makes it a primary occupation. Tailoring, banking and bus driving involve manufacturing or services and are therefore secondary or tertiary occupations.

questions.q: Which of the following is a characteristic of land as a factor of production?
options: It is man-made and can be moved from place to place.
Its supply is fixed and cannot be increased at will.
It is completely free and has no opportunity cost.
Its reward is interest on capital invested.
questions.explanation: Land is a natural factor whose supply is fixed and cannot be increased at will. It is not man-made or movable, and its reward is rent, not interest; it also has an opportunity cost.

questions.q: Which of the following is a disadvantage of division of labour in a factory?
options: Workers may become bored from performing repetitive tasks.
Total output is always lower than when one worker does every task.
Workers cannot become skilled in any particular operation.
Workers require longer training for every task.
questions.explanation: Division of labour can lead to monotony and boredom because a worker repeats a narrow task. It usually shortens training, increases skill in a specific operation, and can raise total output.

questions.q: An exporter in Lagos ships cocoa by sea to a buyer in Rotterdam. Which document, signed on behalf of the shipowner, acknowledges that the goods have been received on board and entitles the holder to claim them on arrival?
questions.explanation: The bill of lading is issued by the shipowner or carrier and serves as a receipt for goods shipped, evidence of the contract of carriage and a document of title. The bill of exchange is used mainly to finance and demand payment, while a certificate of origin shows the source of goods and a shipping note gives instructions for shipment.
